Journal of Applied Machine Learning Research

Deep Learning Approaches for Automated Extraction of Scientific Knowledge

Aiman Zaheen, Jordan Lee, and Priya Nair

Department of Computer Science, State University
aiman.zaheen@example.edu, jordan.lee@example.edu

Received: 2 January 2024; Accepted: 15 February 2024; Published: 1 March 2024
DOI: 10.1234/jamlr.2024.00567

Abstract
This paper presents a lightweight pipeline for extracting structured metadata
and section content from research article PDFs. We evaluate the approach on a
corpus of 200 papers and show it recovers titles, authors, and section
boundaries with high accuracy compared to manual annotation.

Keywords: information extraction, natural language processing, scientific documents

1. Introduction
Research articles are published at a rapid pace, making manual review
increasingly impractical. Automated extraction tools can help researchers
triage and organize the literature efficiently.

2. Methods
We built a rule-based parser that detects section headers using regular
expressions and splits the document body accordingly. The parser also
extracts DOIs, emails, and keyword lists using targeted patterns.

3. Results
Across the evaluation corpus, the parser correctly identified section
boundaries in 92% of documents and extracted a valid DOI in 97% of cases.

4. Discussion
The heuristic approach performs well on articles that follow common
formatting conventions, though highly customized layouts remain a
challenge for future work.

5. Conclusion
We presented a simple and effective approach to extracting structured
information from research articles, suitable for building literature
review tools.

References

[2] Nguyen, T. (2019). Automated metadata extraction from PDFs. Proceedings of the ACM Conference on Digital Libraries, 100-110.
